column3: こんにちはお元気ですか
column6: こんにちは|お元気|です|か
column8: Ogenki desu ka asks how someone is doing.

column1: Toukyou no tenki wa dou desu ka?
column2: How is the weather in Tokyo?
column3: 東京の天気はどうですか
column6: 東京|の|天気|は|どう|です|か
column8: No links Tokyo to its weather; dou desu ka asks what it is like.

column1: San Furanshisuko no tenki wa yoi desu.
column2: The weather in San Francisco is nice.
column3: サンフランシスコの天気はよいです
column6: サン|フランシスコ|の|天気|は|よい|です
column8: Yoi means good or nice. San Furanshisuko is written as two romaji words here.

column1: Watashi ni wa chichi to haha to imouto ga hitori imasu.
column2: I have a father, a mother, and one younger sister.
column3: 私には父と母といもうとが一人います
column6: 私|に|は|父|と|母|と|いもうと|が|一人|います
column8: To joins family members; hitori counts one person. Imasu is the polite form of iru, used for people.

column1: Chichi to haha wa Ookurando ni sunde imasu.
column2: My father and mother live in Oakland.
column3: 父と母はオークランドに住んでいます
column6: 父|と|母|は|オークランド|に|住んで|います
column8: Sumu → sunde + imasu means live / reside. Ni marks where they live.

column1: Demo, imouto wa San Diego ni sunde imasu.
column2: But my younger sister lives in San Diego.
column3: でもいもうとはサンディエゴに住んでいます
column6: でも|いもうと|は|サン|ディエゴ|に|住んで|います
column8: Demo means but. Sumu → sunde imasu describes where someone lives.

column3: 父はろくじゅっさいです
column6: 父|は|ろくじゅっさい|です
column8: Rokujussai means sixty years old. Keep the doubled ss.

column3: いもうとは十八歳です
column6: いもうと|は|十八歳|です
column8: Juuhassai means eighteen years old; hassai uses doubled ss.

column1: Chichi wa kensetsu no shigoto o shite imasu.
column3: 父はけんせつのしごとをしています
column6: 父|は|けんせつ|の|しごと|を|して|います
column8: Suru → shite + imasu describes an occupation. Kensetsu no shigoto means construction work.

column1: Haha wa jimu no shigoto o shite imasu.
column3: 母はじむのしごとをしています
column6: 母|は|じむ|の|しごと|を|して|います
column8: Jimu means office / administrative work here. Shite imasu comes from suru, to do.

column2: My younger sister is a college student.
column3: いもうとは大学生です
column6: いもうと|は|大学生|です

column2: I watch TV with my father.
column8: To means with; miru → mimasu means watch (polite).

column2: I go hiking with my mother.
column3: 母とハイキングに行きます
column6: 母|と|ハイキング|に|行きます
column8: Iku → ikimasu means go (polite). Haikingu ni iku means go hiking.

column2: I play games with my younger sister.
column3: いもうととゲームをします
column6: いもうと|と|ゲーム|を|します
column8: Suru → shimasu means do (polite). Geemu o suru means play games.

column1: Sore dewa, minasan ni oai suru no o tanoshimi ni shite imasu.
column2: I look forward to meeting you all.
column3: それでは皆さんにお会いするのを楽しみにしています
column6: それ|では|皆さん|に|お会い|する|の|を|楽しみ|に|して|います
column8: Oai suru is a polite expression for meeting. No makes meeting you all into a noun phrase. Tanoshimi ni shite imasu means look forward to.

column3: よろしくお願いします
column6: よろしく|お願い|します
column8: A polite closing requesting goodwill; the English translation depends on context.
Yori means from in a letter signature.
